title: F7 proponent: K1/K2 legacy keys (PALIMPSEST + ABSCISSA + KRYPTOS) as substitution candidates
hypothesis_summary: K1, K2, K3 are public-fact-solved with construction-attested keywords PALIMPSEST (K1), ABSCISSA (K2), and KRYPTOS-mixed alphabets (all of K1-K3). Sanborn's two-systems claim does NOT guarantee K1-K3 keys apply to K4, but the keyword family's documented reuse is the strongest WEAK analogy available. The proponent reading enumerates these legacy keys as substitution candidates composed with a keyed columnar transposition.

provenance_items.quote_or_summary: PALIMPSEST (K1 cipher keyword), ABSCISSA (K2 cipher keyword), KRYPTOS (alphabet keyword for K1-K3) — registered in TIER_KRYPTOS_PLAINTEXT_LEGACY.

composition_templates.rationale: Sub + columnar with legacy keyword pool.
Beaufort sub + columnar with legacy keyword pool.

constraints: Allowed keyword pool restricted to legacy-keyword set.
caveats: Sanborn's two-systems disclosure means K1-K3 keys are NOT guaranteed to apply directly. This pack tests the keyword-family analogy, not the specific keyword.

Compiler limitation: the bridge currently uses default AZ alphabet for keyword-pair families; KRYPTOS as 'alphabet' role hint is logged but the alphabet keyword machinery is not yet wired through this emitter.
